chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Al-Abd Al-Salih (peace be upon him), who said:

A mother of the child of his father asked him, so she said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! I would like to ask you about something but I am too embarrassed from it'. So he said: 'Ask me and do not be embarrassed'. She said, 'The blood of menstruation hit my clothes, so I washed them, but its effects did not go away'. So he said: 'Dye it with Mishq (a dye) until it gets mixed up and goes away'.

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of the child; a concubine who bears her master's child
key_terms.مِشْقٍ: A type of dye or pigment used to change the color of fabric
key_terms.يَخْتَلِطَ: To mix or blend (referring to the color of the stain blending with the dye)

ai.seo_question: How to purify clothes stained with menstrual blood according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical jurisprudence of the seventh Imam, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him), regarding the purification of garments stained by menstrual blood. It illustrates the Shia legal principle that if the physical substance (majmud) is removed, the remaining visible trace (athar) can be rendered ritually pure through dyeing (tabkhir) with 'mishq' (a type of dye or pigment) until the color blends indistinguishably, facilitating ease in prayer.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Abd Al-Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), said,

‘A mother of the child of hisasws fatherasws asked himasws, so she said, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! I would like to ask youasws about something but I am too embarrassed from it’. So heasws said:’ Ask measws and do not be embarrassed’. She said, ‘The blood of menstruation (Haydh) hit my clothes, so I washed them, but its effects did not go away’. So heasws said: ‘Dye it with Mishq (a dye) until it gets mixed up and goes away’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from virtuous servant (of Allah) who has said the following:

“Once a mother of the child of his father asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, I like to ask you a question but I feel shy. He (the Imam) said, ‘Ask and do not feel shy.’ She said, ‘My clothes have come in contact with blood of Hayd (menses) and I wash them, but its marks do not go away. He (the Imam) said, ‘Dye them with Mishq (a kind of dye) to mix its color and it will go away.’”
